paper.title_en: Stellar-evolution systematic biases on $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ constraints from the primordial-black-hole mass gap
paper.abstract_en: The $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ reaction determines helium-burning carbon-oxygen core masses and sets the pair-instability-supernova mass-gap boundary, which limits the maximum mass of stellar-origin primordial black holes. Gravitational-wave population analyses using GWTC-4 report a low-spin-black-hole upper cutoff at $68.5^{+19.8}_{-18.5}\,M_\odot$, implying a low astrophysical S-factor $S_{300}\approx 108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$, in tension with canonical nuclear-astrophysics evaluations. However, stellar-evolution systematic uncertainties from metallicity, rotation, and mass-loss prescriptions remain poorly quantified. Here we use the MESA stellar-evolution code to construct a three-dimensional parameter grid disentangling these coupled effects. We show that metallicity-dependent winds dominate helium-core retention; rotation suppresses carbon consumption via centrifugal cooling and meridional mixing; different mass-loss prescriptions produce $8$-$10\,M_\odot$ offsets in the black-hole-mass-gap edge. A parameter combination $Z\approx10^{-3}$, moderate rotation $ω/ω_\mathrm{crit}=0.4$, and optically-thin C15 winds reproduces the GWTC-4 inferred maximum primordial-black-hole mass for $S_{300}=108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$. The canonical $45\,M_\odot$ gap boundary represents an overlapping statistical intersection of black-hole-population distributions rather than a universal physical threshold. Our framework provides a pathway to jointly constrain nuclear-reaction rates, stellar-evolution physics, and gravitational-wave-source populations.
